- When sentiment is negative or mixed in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 5–10% for 30-day horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high.
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), model overreacts; apply downward bias of 3–5% for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is consistently positive but price is falling, model may lag; adjust forecast to match recent low trend, not peak.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is below 70% of 30-day moving average, model often overestimates; apply 10–15% downward correction.
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.00 or negative values, model tends to ignore sentiment; force a 5–10% downward adjustment if sentiment is weak or negative.
